clue.text: Chap almost daring to speak Chinese

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: almost means the word daring stops one letter short of its end

explanation.surface: A fellow nearly plucks up the courage to try speaking Chinese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter G from DARING, leaving DARIN; 'to speak' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the principal spoken language of China, the standard form of Chinese.

clue.text: Cheese made the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the word made is to be read backwards

explanation.surface: A cheese that was produced badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns MADE back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a round Dutch cheese, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Ash found by Ella on the stage

definitions.meaning: ash is the burnt remains of a fire, a sense shared by the answer

definitions.text: found by Ella on the stage
definitions.meaning: placed beside the name Ella it makes the heroine of a stage pantomime

explanation.surface: Ash discovered by a girl named Ella in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The pantomime heroine Cinderella is this word followed by ELLA, so it is literally found beside Ella on the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinder is a piece of burnt coal or wood, so ash and cinder are near synonyms.

clue.text: Ingrid can be found on river with FBI agent

parts.note: taken as written
a G-man is American slang for a federal agent of the FBI

explanation.surface: An actress named Ingrid turns up on a river alongside a federal agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' and 'found on' are link words; in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid Bergman was the Swedish film star, so her first name points to her surname.

clue.text: Sell Spanish separatists, reportedly found feuding

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the noun answer: a state of prolonged feuding

indicators.note: reportedly says the pieces before it are only heard, not spelt

parts.note: to sell is to vend; ETA was the Basque separatist group in Spain

explanation.surface: Selling out Spanish separatists is said to have led to feuding.
explanation.walkthrough: VEND + ETA said together sound like the answer, which has a double T.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long blood feud, so feuding describes exactly that state of hostility.

clue.text: Hideaway with grass on, which may be open all hours

definitions.text: which may be open all hours

parts.note: a corner is a secluded spot, a hideaway
to grass is British slang for informing on someone, to shop them

explanation.surface: A secluded spot with grass on top that may be open around the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the informer's word sits under the hideaway. Open All Hours was a British sitcom set in a small local shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A British corner shop is a small local store known for long opening times, as in the sitcom Open All Hours.

clue.text: Resulted in bell ringing loud note

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the bell is put round the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A bell's ringing produced a loud note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like the sound of the bell, but it means surrounding: BELL goes round F and E. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Befell means happened or came about, which is what an event that resulted did.

clue.text: Tough policy on complicated land hire

indicators.note: complicated suggests the letters of land hire are tangled up and need sorting

explanation.surface: A firm stance on a messy business of renting out land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges LANDHIRE; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard line is an uncompromising, unyielding stance, a tough policy in politics.

clue.text: Wear down the Queen with long poem

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
an ode is a lyric poem, often a lengthy one

explanation.surface: The monarch is worn out by a lengthy piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water wears down rock.

clue.text: First man to be a mother

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: The first man to become a mother, an absurd notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Adam is the first human being, the first man created.

clue.text: Fido's meal's a mess

definitions.meaning: Fido is a stock dog's name, so his meal is the dog's food
British slang for a botched, chaotic muddle

explanation.surface: The dog's food has made a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog's dinner is everyday British slang for a shambles.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is a pet's food bowl; idiomatically it is a muddle or shambles.

clue.text: He was a king just half a day

parts.note: R is rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: just half keeps only the front half of the day named, cutting off the rest

parts.note: Thursday is a day of the week

explanation.surface: A monarch whose reign lasted only half a day.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first four of THURSDAY's eight letters survive; 'was' is a link word, and the surface leans on King Arthur.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a man's name, so the pronoun stands for him; he was the legendary king of Camelot.

clue.text: Doubt when he gets a non-U situation

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: non-U says the word situation must lose its letter U

explanation.surface: Uncertainty arises when a man finds himself in an unrefined position.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper-class; here it says remove U from SITUATION, leaving SITATION. 'when', 'gets' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitation is a pause from uncertainty, so it is a form of doubt.

clue.text: Despite what's been said, a rat fell out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of a rat fell are disordered

explanation.surface: Whatever anyone said, a rodent tumbled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ARATFELL.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase after all means in spite of anything said or expected before.

clue.text: Harmonious movement in dance

definitions.meaning: moving in unison, in step together
a ballroom dance in quick march time popular in the early twentieth century

explanation.surface: Moving harmoniously in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one step together suggests unison, and the one-step is also a ragtime-era dance.

clue.text: Supports one with dress in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray tells us the letters of one and dress are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone backs a person whose clothes are messed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two fodder words; 'in disarray' rearranges ONEDRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to back or approve publicly, to support.

clue.text: Friend from a city in Somerset nearly found beside the tub

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, a county in south-west England

indicators.note: nearly says the phrase falls short by its final letter

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A pal from a Somerset city is almost discovered next to the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH + MATE gives BATHMATE; 'nearly' removes the final E. Bath is a spa city in Somerset, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath mat is the small rug laid beside the bathtub to step out onto.

clue.text: It's been read variously in Scotland

definitions.note: a place-locator: something found in Scotland stands for the city

indicators.note: variously means the letters of been read are set out in another order

explanation.surface: Something has been interpreted in different ways north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variously' rearranges BEENREAD; 'It's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a major city on the north-east coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Of a British poet's broadcast in Corby

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of in Corby are spread about

explanation.surface: A poem by an English writer goes out on air in a Northamptonshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' stands for 'is'; 'broadcast' rearranges INCORBY. Corby is a town in Northamptonshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Byronic means relating to Lord Byron, the Romantic poet, or his brooding style.

clue.text: Anniversary of Sir Robin joining Labour

parts.note: labour is the process of giving birth
Sir Robin Day was a famous British television political interviewer

explanation.surface: An anniversary of a knighted man joining the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the political party, but it is childbirth. Sir Robin Day was a well-known British TV interviewer; 'joining' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday is the yearly anniversary of the day a person was born.

clue.text: More than one plant is about to grow

indicators.note: about means going round, so is surrounds the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
to rise is to grow or increase

explanation.surface: A plant is on the point of growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are flowering plants; the plural form matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Sword held by artist on jetty

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a pier is a jetty

explanation.surface: A sword in the possession of a painter on a jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist; 'held by' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed sword used for thrusting.

clue.text: Turn, or turned, junk east

indicators.note: turned tells us the word or is to be reversed

parts.note: tat is British slang for cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Spin, or be spun, while discarding east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like part of the definition, but reverses OR to RO. Tat is British slang for tasteless junk.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn round on an axis.

clue.text: No beautifier of public places

parts.note: someone who far from making streets prettier spoils them by dropping rubbish

explanation.definitionFit: A litter lout is a person who carelessly drops rubbish in public, the opposite of a beautifier.

clue.text: Left words for bride and groom in Venice

definitions.note: a place-locator: something found in Venice stands for the island

parts.note: I do is what each partner says in a wedding service

explanation.surface: Instructions left for a couple getting married in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I do' is the vow each partner speaks at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lido is the long barrier island beach resort in the Venetian lagoon.

clue.text: Woollies half removed, revealing whoppers!

indicators.note: half removed tells us the front half of the word Woollies is cut away

explanation.surface: Half the woollens are taken off, showing great big fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: Woollies has eight letters; removing the first four leaves the rest. 'revealing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoppers is informal for big lies, outrageous untruths.

clue.text: Recall first girl to swallow rubber stamp

indicators.note: to swallow means to take inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
to rubber-stamp is to OK, to approve

explanation.surface: A girl is called back after gulping down an official stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swallow' is the container signal; OK is the informal word for approve.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call up a memory, so it means to recall.

clue.text: Bankrupt there in India

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: IND is the international abbreviation for India
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone went broke out there in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Being in the red means a debit balance, shown in red ink in old ledgers.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the red is to owe money, so it stands for being bankrupt or in debt.
